scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation at Walmart. Let me start by going through what happened step by step to understand my actions and the reactions of others. First, I'm a 24-year-old male working at Walmart for the summer. My job is mainly in the back room dealing with inventory, which includes lifting heavy boxes. One of my co-workers is a woman in her early to mid-30s, who seems physically fit and doesn't have any obvious disabilities. She approached me and asked for help lifting a heavy box. I agreed, thinking we'd do a team lift. But when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me instead of helping. I asked if she was ready, and she said it just needed to go into a bin about 4 feet high. I offered to help, but she said it was too heavy for her and asked me to lift it into the bin alone. I responded that I'm happy to help if she's having trouble, but I'm not going to lift all her heavy boxes while she stands there. She got upset and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team, who's not my boss but the most senior person directing us, came to me and said he spoke to her. He told me that the next time someone asks for help, I need to help them because that's part of being a team. I clarified what happened, explaining that she didn't help and just wanted me to do all the work. I also mentioned that if she can't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job, and I'm not the designated heavy lifter. I suggested discussing it further with HR if needed and then stormed off feeling annoyed. So, was I the asshole here? It seems like two against one, with the co-worker and the head guy against me. But I need to think about whether my actions were appropriate or if I overreacted. First, I agreed to help her, which is good. But when she didn't help and just wanted me to do all the work, I felt it was unfair. I expressed that I'm happy to help if she's struggling, but I'm not her personal heavy lifter. That seems reasonable because teamwork should involve both people contributing. However, the head guy told me that helping is part of being a team, which makes sense in a team environment. Maybe I should have been more accommodating, even if it felt one-sided. On the other hand, I don't want to set a precedent where I'm always the one doing the heavy lifting while others stand by. I also need to consider the workplace dynamics. The head guy is more senior, so his feedback carries weight. Dismissing his advice or storming off might have come across as disrespectful or uncooperative, which could affect my standing on the team. Additionally, the co-worker might have felt disrespected when I refused to lift the box alone. She might have been under pressure or genuinely struggling, even if it didn't seem like it. My response could have been perceived as dismissive or unwilling to support a teammate. On the flip side, I stood up for myself by not letting someone take advantage of my willingness to help. It's important to set boundaries to avoid burnout or resentment. But I also need to balance that with being a team player. Maybe a better approach would have been to acknowledge her request, offer assistance in a way that's fair, and perhaps discuss the workload with the team leader privately instead of confronting her in front of others. That way, I maintain teamwork while also addressing my concerns. In the end, I think there's a middle ground. While I wasn't entirely wrong to expect mutual effort, I could have handled the situation more diplomatically to maintain positive team dynamics.
